angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 570,474 km at 153.11 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.5313 +/- 0.0080 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 153.11 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.82 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Sun et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-411 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...624A..15S/abstract): 570,474 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.87 +/- 0.039 solar masses from Sun et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-411 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...624A..15S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4837 +/- 149.59 K from TICv8, the stellar temperature of Kepler-411 c's parameter set from TICv8 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: TICv8, the stellar temperature of Kepler-411 c's parameter set from TICv8 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-411.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.550, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
